events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SVREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
West central Hidalgo County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 417 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 4 miles south of
Portal, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Rodeo and Animas.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Northern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Some low-water
crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 255 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause small stream flooding. Between 0.5
and 0.8 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northern Cochise County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 15 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait, City and Borough of
Juneau, Eastern Chichagof Island, and Glacier Bay.

* WHEN...From 9 PM this evening to 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will quickly increase overnight Monday
into Tuesday morning, with the strongest gusts peaking through
midday Tuesday. Strong wind gusts will continue through Tuesday
night before decreasing into Wednesday morning.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and 12
inches, with the greater amounts more likely at higher elevations.

* WHERE...Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 10 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads. Areas of low visibility especially in heavier snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snowfall will begin late this evening and
continue through late Tuesday evening. Temperatures will cool to
and below freezing late this evening, changing a mix of snow and
rain to solidly snowfall. Snow accumulations will be greater at
higher elevations. There is uncertainty for lower elevation snow
accumulations which will depend on how snow levels change over
time.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Additional snow accumulations between 2 and 4
inches.

* WHERE...Northern Susitna Valley.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will continue over the Northern Susitna
Valley this afternoon with steady snowfall continuing along the
Parks Highway from north of Talkeetna across Broad Pass through
this evening. The snow is then expected to taper off by tonight.
Another round of light snow is possible during the day Tuesday.
